title: Lie Detection via Semantic Consistency Across Paraphrase Pairs

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain: paraphrase consistency as honesty signal could enable cheap honesty audits. However, the core assumption (lies show lower paraphrase consistency) is unvalidated and may not hold for capable models that maintain consistent fictions. The theory link has an untested assumption at its core.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Simple methodology: generate paraphrased questions, collect responses, compute embedding cosine similarity. API-based for both generation and embeddings. Beginners can execute this with standard tooling (OpenAI embeddings API, basic Python).

narrow_scope.reasoning: Clean single experiment: factual questions with known answers, 10 paraphrase variants each, consistency measurement. Well-defined deliverable (consistency scores for correct vs. incorrect answers). Easily within 30 hours.
